BP (+0.27%) and Nvidia (+0.85%) also finished green. ResMed (-2.52%) and Republic Services (-2.37%) stayed our two soft spots (rate-sensitive), but both sit safely above their automatic safety-sells. On Microsoft: your approved plan said buy ONLY on a calm dip into $515-522 and do NOT chase at $525+. Microsoft closed at $525.18 — above that line — so, exactly per your plan, I did not buy and did not trim the S&P floor. The plan stays ready for a real dip. latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady and green — no changes, and I passed on Microsoft again (still too hot to chase)
latest_messages.body: Noon risk check — no trades. We're UP ~$739 today (+0.78%) and beating the S&P 500 so far (it's +0.57%). Our two weakest holds this morning, ResMed and Republic Services, both bounced back, so they're further from their safety-sells now (cushions ~4.6% and ~4.9%, up from ~3.3%/2.8% at the open). I looked at Microsoft one more time: it cooled a bit from its morning spike but is still ~$525 — about 8% above its 50-day trend line, still stretched. My rule is to buy quality names on a CALM entry, not chase a pop; buying up here would park our safety-net sell right under a short-term peak (how we've been shaken out before). Its earnings are ~Oct 28, so there's no rush. Nice side effect of waiting: I didn't sell any of our S&P 500 floor, keeping full market exposure on an up day — part of why we're ahead of the index right now. Next check-in: the 3:00 CT close with your daily scorecard. Cash ~$10.5k (~11%, on target); 0 of 3 weekly buys used; slot still reserved for Microsoft.

latest_messages.headline: Open: no trade yet — held off on Microsoft because it jumped too far, too fast
latest_messages.body: Market opened; everything's healthy and we're about flat (+$34). I planned to buy Microsoft but decided NOT to at the open — on purpose. The twist: Microsoft got even better news overnight (a fresh upgrade to Buy, $665 target, plus Wells Fargo naming it a top idea), which is great for the story — but it made the stock gap up +2.7% while the market barely moved. My rule is to buy quality names on a calm, steady entry, not chase a one-morning pop to a fresh high (that's how we've been shaken out before). Bonus: by not buying, I didn't have to sell any of our S&P 500 floor, so we actually kept a touch MORE market exposure on an up day. I'll re-check at midday — if Microsoft settles instead of sprinting, I'll buy a ~10-12% starter with a −7% safety net, funded by trimming one S&P 500 slice. If it keeps running, I wait. Cash ~$10.5k (on target); 0 of 3 weekly buys used; slot still reserved for Microsoft.
